holidays.name: National French Bread Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the baguette and its crackly crust and fluffy, chewy middle. Tear off a hunk, slather it with butter, and call it a celebration.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It celebrates French bread's long role in French cooking and daily life. The modern baguette took shape in the 1920s, after a French labor law limited bakers' early-morning hours and favored a thinner loaf that baked faster.
holidays.funFact: In 2022, UNESCO added the artisanal know-how and culture of the baguette to its list of intangible cultural heritage.

holidays.name: National Common Courtesy Day
holidays.description: A reminder to be polite. Hold the door, say please and thank you, let someone merge in front of you, and put your phone away at dinner.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance dates to the early 2000s. It encourages small acts of everyday consideration.
holidays.funFact: It falls on the first day of spring, which makes it a good day for a fresh start with your manners.

holidays.name: National Fragrance Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate scents. Spritz your favorite perfume or cologne, light a candle, or sniff your way through a flower shop to mark the first blush of spring.
holidays.origin: The fragrance industry promoted the day as a way to celebrate scent. It is an unofficial observance with no government status.
holidays.funFact: Smell is closely tied to memory, so a single whiff of a familiar scent can bring back a moment from years ago.
